title: Marcus by Goldman Sachs, Money Movement & Reconciliation, Analyst, Draper, UT/ Richardson, TX
description:
Marcus by Goldman Sachs
As the online consumer banking business of Goldman Sachs, Marcus operates as a digital bank, providing high-yield savings accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to individual consumers. Marcus combines Goldman Sachs' over 150 years of expertise with intuitive digital experiences, focusing on value, transparency, and simplicity for its millions of customers, and is recognized as the largest pure online bank, delivering a fully digital experience without physical branches.

  • Partner with stakeholders to make improvements and document workflows.
  • Work with leadership to ensure deliverables are provided timely.
  • Prepare detailed communication materials, both presentations and memos, for senior leadership.
  • Proactively resolve potential issues, with escalation as appropriate.

  • General understanding of basic money movement process flows
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree; preferably in Accounting or Business Administrative

title: Construction Inspector – Waterline, Sewer and Pavement Restoration
description:
Construction Inspector - Waterline, Sewer and Pavement Restoration – Cleveland, Ohio

Intertek, a leading provider of quality and safety solutions to many of the world’s top-recognized brands and companies, is actively seeking a Construction Inspector - Waterline, Sewer and Pavement Restoration to join our Professional Service Industries (PSI) team in Cleveland, Ohio. This is a fantastic opportunity to grow a versatile career in architectural, engineering, and construction (A/E/C) industry.

Professional Service Industries, Inc. (Intertek-PSI) is a leading US based provider of construction assurance, testing and inspection in civil and commercial construction. Our broad service offering includes construction materials testing, geotechnical services, environmental engineering, industrial hygiene, and specialty testing.

What are we looking for?

The Construction Inspector - Waterline, Sewer and Pavement Restoration is responsible for ensuring quality, and compliance on critical infrastructure projects.

Salary & Benefits Information

In addition to competitive compensation packages, when working with Intertek you can expect benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, 401(k) with company match, generous vacation / sick time (PTO), tuition reimbursement and more.

What you’ll do:

  • Inspect and monitor waterline, sewer and associated infrastructure installation, repair and replacement projects for compliance with plans, specifications and standards.
  • Oversee pavement restoration activities ensuring proper materials, compaction and finish quality.
  • Document daily progress, prepare inspection reports and communicate findings to the supervisor and the client.
  • At times, perform materials testing on concrete, soils and asphalt as needed.

This position outline is a general guideline and does not represent all encompassing details. The position assumes that the incumbent has both the mental and physical requirements to carry out the above defined duties.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications:

  • Proven experience in waterline and sewer construction as well as pavement restoration inspections.
  • Strong knowledge of construction methods, materials and safety protocol.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable driving record (required)

Preferred Requirements & Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • 6 months of construction related experience
  • ACI Certification
  • NECEPT Certification - Not necessary but preferred

Intertek: Total Quality. Assured.

campaigns. In addition to copywriting, you will be responsible for assisting with the project management of marketing materials for the Noble House collection alongside an in-house creative team of graphic designers.

title: Fleet Maintenance Fueler Washer
location: West Valley City, UT, United States
description:
2211 S 2000 W, West Valley City, UT 84119

What’s the Job?
Ready to accelerate your career while helping our customers move forward? As a Fleet Maintenance Fueler Washer at Penske, you’ll do exactly that. You will make sure vehicles are fueled, clean and safe before they hit the road again. You will be the face of Penske—the person greeting our customers when they arrive and the one sending them off with a smile.

Why join Penske as a Fleet Maintenance Fueler Washer, you ask? It’s simple. Maybe you’ve always had an interest in vehicle maintenance but haven’t had the chance to pursue it. This is the perfect place to start. No experience is required. We will introduce you to our vehicle maintenance processes. We will teach you how to use our leading-edge technology. In fact, the training and experience you get here will help you advance to become a technician. And you’ll get to do that learning at a company that offers career stability and competitive benefits. Talk about an amazing opportunity.

It’s about going above and beyond for our customers—the way Penske goes above and beyond for you. It’s about building meaningful relationships. It’s about keeping our customers moving forward.

Main Responsibilities:
• Greeting our customers and making sure they have a great experience as you fuel and wash vehicles
• Performing vehicle readiness inspections to make sure tires, fluids, and other basic maintenance items are done
• Helping make sure our facilities are clean, safe environments for our customers and associates
• Building your skills through training and hands-on coaching to perform minor repairs such as installing mounted tires, replacing or rotating tires and performing preventive maintenance repairs
• Completing other projects and tasks as assigned by supervisor

Why Penske is for You:
• Competitive starting salary
• Shift Premiums - 2nd shift ($2.50), 3rd shift ($3.50), Weekends ($2.50)
• Career stability
• Opportunity for growth
• Excellent benefits, including lots of time off
• Strong, well-rounded training programs
• Advanced vehicle maintenance technology
• Location and schedule flexibility
General Requirements:
• High school diploma, equivalent, or prior work experience preferred
• Valid driver’s license required
• Excellent customer service and communication skills
• The ability to work well as part of a team
• The ability and willingness to work outside
• Basic mechanical ability and tool usage (preferred)
• Basic computer skills
• The associate will be required to understand and comply with specific instructions, guidelines, rules, regulations, or other information established by Penske management
• The associate must be able to perform all work adhering to DOT, OSHA, and all Penske safety and maintenance policies; including but not limited to the correct selection and use of appropriate tools, PPE, machine guarding, and established best safety practice.
• Regular, predictable, full attendance is an essential function of the job
• As this position requires driving Penske and customer vehicles, it is regulated by the DOT and requires a current driver qualification file to be maintained as required by the role. The driver qualification file includes: an annual motor vehicle records (MVR) check, a successfully completed DOT Physical, and Safety Performance History records request from prior employers in the last 3 years. Additionally, CDL holders will have a DOT Drug Screening within 30 days of start and subject to a FMCSA Clearinghouse review.
• Willingness to work the required schedule, work at the specific location required, complete Penske employment application, submit to a background screening (to include criminal checks, past employment and education), the ability to pass a drug screen and physical as required by the Department of Transportation, and potential travel within a near geography for training are required.

This position is regulated by the Department of Transportation or designated as safety sensitive by the company, and the ability to work in a constant state of alertness and in a safe manner is required. Associates must have the ability to accept responsibility for their own safety, as well as the safety of others.
Physical Requirements: The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
• While performing the duties of this job, the associate will be required to move frequently, stand, walk, climb, bend, and sit for extended length of time throughout their scheduled working period.
• The associate is required to use their hands on a routine and daily basis to grasp, reach, touch, handle, feel, and/or otherwise operate required tools or controls.
• The associate must be able to work safely at heights using applicable ladders and elevated working platforms.
• The associate must be able to safely work in all weather conditions.
• Given the frequent movement of large trucks through the workplace, the associate must be able to see and hear in order to safely navigate the work environment.
• The associate must be able to regularly lift and/or move up to 50lbs/23kg and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100lbs/45kg. This position also requires the ability to push/pull truck tires on a regular basis that exceed 100 pounds.

Pay: $21.00/hr
Shift: Monday-Friday 2:30pm-11pm

Penske is an Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Water Resources Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
description:
This Opportunity

WSP USA hosts hundreds of internships across the United States to gain hands-on, meaningful work experience to enhance their education and professional aptitude. Our interns gain exposure to real projects while working side by side with senior staff. Through our Developing Professionals Network, interns gain mentorship, networking opportunities and lifelong career connections.

Our Earth & Environment Team is seeking a full-time Water Resources Engineering Intern - Summer 2027 to work out of our Brentwood, TN office. The following locations will also be considered: Knoxville, TN and Birmingham, AL. This temporary position is seeking individuals currently enrolled in an Undergraduate or Graduate degree program.

This internship will be part of the WSP Summer Internship Program. As a summer intern, you have the opportunity to participate in our 12-week program scheduled to start on May 17th, 2027. The individual start date of the internship may be flexible.

Your Impact

  • Support a variety of engineering tasks with the goal to develop technical, social, and ethical skills.

  • Learn basic principles of Water Resources Engineering.

  • Assist with project research, field work, and preliminary design calculations and analysis.

  • Support preparation of final design plans, special provisions, and cost estimates.

  • Assist in collecting and maintaining project documentation.

  • Complete training on assigned tasks.

  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.

  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

  • Please note that there is no relocation or housing assistance associated with this internship.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Actively enrolled in an accredited Civil Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related Undergraduate program with an anticipated graduation date of August 2027 or later.

  • Must be 18 or older.

  • Demonstrated interest in Water Resources Engineering, or related field, and have a strong desire to advance skills related to WSP’s work and projects.

  • Competent interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.

  • Capable of taking direction from leadership, mentors, and managers to executive projects.

  • Basic proficiency with technical writing, office automation, software, spreadsheets, technology, and tools.

  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

  • Authorization to work in the United States at the start of the internship.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Actively enrolled in an accredited Civil Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related Masters or PhD program with an anticipated graduation date of August 2027 or later.

  • Experience using Civil 3D, ArcGIS, HEC-RAS, HEC HMS, hydraulic modeling and calculations, MathCAD, OpenRoads, InRoads, or Blubeam Software.

  • Prior internship and leadership involvement on campus.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (all locations): $22.17 - $29.96

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

title: Early Talent Specialist
description:
What if you could redefine what’s possible? With us, you can.

You want Purpose. Growth. Opportunity. People who get it.
We are the home of ambitious, passionate, and innovative world shapers.
With an unmatched breadth and depth of engineering, advisory and science-based expertise, our global minds unite to power local solutions.
We are pathfinders and impact makers.
We are Visioneers.
We are WSP.

The Opportunity

At WSP, the people we hire help shape communities and advance humanity. As an Early Talent Specialist, you’ll help build the next generation of professionals by connecting emerging talent with opportunities where they can learn, contribute and grow.
You’ll own early career recruitment from intake through hire while bringing our regional campus strategy to life through meaningful events, candidate engagement and talent pipelines. It’s an opportunity to combine hands-on recruiting with campus programming and build an experience that helps great early career talent see a future with WSP.

Your Impact

  • Lead end-to-end recruitment for assigned early talent positions, from role intake and sourcing through assessment, selection, offer acceptance and handoff.
  • Partner with hiring stakeholders to define role requirements, success criteria, assessment methods, timelines and selection responsibilities so recruitment starts with a clear path forward.
  • Assess and engage applicants using consistent, evidence-based criteria, providing well-supported candidate recommendations and maintaining momentum throughout the recruitment process.
  • Bring campus programs to life by coordinating career fairs, recruitment events, campaigns and information sessions, including schedules, materials, internal representatives and day-of-event delivery.
  • Build and nurture relationships with students, new graduates and other early career candidates, creating active talent pipelines aligned with regional hiring priorities.
  • Convert engagement into talent through timely post-event follow-up that moves qualified prospects toward applications, interviews, hires or future opportunities.
  • Collaborate with business representatives, campus ambassadors and internal partners to deliver a consistent and inclusive candidate experience.
  • Use recruitment, event and pipeline insights to strengthen candidate communications, assessment consistency, recruitment processes and future campus programming.

The Skills That Set You Apart

  • Experience managing end-to-end recruitment, with the ability to move confidently from intake and candidate assessment through selection and offer acceptance.
  • Experience supporting early career, campus or high-volume recruitment programs, including career fairs, recruitment campaigns, information sessions or related candidate engagement activities.
  • Fluency in both French and English, written and spoken, to communicate effectively with candidates, hiring stakeholders and partners across Canada.
  • Strong recruitment judgment, including the ability to translate business requirements into clear success criteria and make evidence-based candidate recommendations.
  • Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with hiring stakeholders, candidates and internal partners while keeping decisions and recruitment activity moving.
  • Strong organizational and event coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple requisitions, schedules, events, stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Experience maintaining accurate recruitment documentation and candidate records in an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) throughout the recruitment lifecycle.
  • A candidate-first approach, with the ability to build relationships with emerging talent, maintain engagement and create a professional and consistent recruitment experience.

Why Choose WSP?

We exist to shape communities to advance humanity. The brightest engineers, advisors and scientists from across the globe call WSP home.
  • Proudly Canadian – we are a Top 100 Employer in Canada for 2026.
  • A global community of brilliant minds – your next idea, mentor, or opportunity is always within reach.
  • Limitless opportunities start here. Whether it’s across the country or around the globe, we help you tailor your role to match your ambition — because your growth drives ours.
  • Flexible work, real balance – we recognize the importance of balance in our lives and encourage you to prioritize the balance in yours.
#WeAreWSP

Make Your Mark with WSP

Help shape where great careers begin.

title: Metallurgical Technician
description:
ABOUT YOU

You will have a keen eye for detail, with a passion for producing accurate, high-quality work. You'll be confident and comfortable working with laboratory equipment to carry out microscopic evaluation, corrosion testing and chemical analysis. As a collaborative team player, you'll communicate effectively with colleagues and clients, thrive in a quality-driven environment, and be committed to continuous improvement and delivering excellent results.

Required skills and experience:

  • Good IT literacy skills
  • Degree or qualification in sciences or another technical discipline.
  • Clear and effective communication skills

This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-established laboratory where you'll play a key role in delivering high-quality metallurgical testing and analysis services. Working alongside an experienced team, you'll be involved in the preparation, testing and evaluation of metal samples for a diverse range of industries, helping clients make informed engineering and manufacturing decisions. In return, you'll have the opportunity to further develop your technical expertise, work with modern laboratory equipment and techniques, and contribute to a business that values quality, collaboration and professional development.

Key activities:

  • Metallurgical preparation of metal samples in line with specifications, including sectioning, grinding, polishing and etching of samples.

  • Microscopic Evaluation of samples to specifications.

  • Performance of corrosion tests.

  • Chemical analysis of metal samples.

  • Report analysis findings in an accurate and concise manner.

Join Intertek and become part of our global network of inspiring and entrepreneurial colleagues. We are a global family that values diversity and we thrive working together with precision, pace, and passion. We are working to make the world Ever Better, ensuring the quality, safety and sustainability of products and services used by millions of people around the world.

  • Competitive salary/benefits
  • Development and career opportunities around the Globe
  • Working in a highly motivated team and dynamic working environment

We do not discriminate against applicants, and all qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

title: Senior Hybrid Test Engineer - Playwright C#
description:
Planit are world leaders in application testing and quality engineering. We provide solutions that support organisations to deliver high quality systems, applications, and IT architecture.

Planit is now a proud NRI company and part of a global movement to deliver a sustainable and secure future through better Information Technology exchanges. Our team offer expert consultancy, bespoke services, tailored training and unique solutions to complex projects. Specialising in digital quality, Planit have a geographic footprint across many continents, with 1700+ permanent employees and have been recognised in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Application Testing Services.

Our values and ethos are focused on an intrinsic connection to our people, the awareness of our environment and our pursuit to be better than yesterday. We continue to lead the industry with unrivalled ideas, ability, and a quest to discern paradigms.

About the Role

We're seeking a hands-on Functional Test Engineer with strong Playwright automation and C# coding experience to join our team in Western Australia.

You'll work across both manual functional testing and test automation, with a strong focus on developing and maintaining automated tests using Playwright and C#.

We're looking for someone who is technically hands-on, comfortable writing automation code and capable of contributing to reliable, maintainable automated testing solutions.

Australian Citizenship is mandatory, with eligibility to obtain Baseline Security Clearance.


What You’ll Do

  • Design, develop and maintain automated test scripts using Playwright and C#.

  • Perform functional, integration, regression and end-to-end testing.

  • Write clean, reusable and maintainable automation code.

  • Develop and enhance automated test coverage within existing testing frameworks.

  • Investigate and troubleshoot automation failures, application defects and testing issues.

  • Collaborate with developers, testers and technical teams to improve testing quality and efficiency.

  • Contribute to test planning, execution, defect management and reporting.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong hands-on Playwright automation experience using C#.

  • Proven C# coding skills, with the ability to independently write, maintain and debug automated test scripts.

  • Solid functional testing experience, including manual test design, execution and defect management.

  • Experience developing automated regression and end-to-end test scenarios.

  • Good understanding of test automation frameworks, coding practices and reusable test components.

  • Experience with API testing, CI/CD pipelines or Azure DevOps would be advantageous.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.

  • Australian Citizenship is mandatory, with eligibility to obtain Baseline Security Clearance.

  • Must be based in Western Australia.

Culture and Benefits

We believe in fostering a culture where our people are rewarded for the work they do and looked after from their first day at Planit! With us, you'll experience:

  • Opportunities to grow your skills vertically and horizontally
  • Take advantage of a world class training and development programme
  • True flexible working initiatives
  • Joining an organisation where innovation is at the heart of what we do.
  • Career development initiatives in place so you can be your best self.
  • Wellness activities, staff discounts, free LinkedIn Learning licences, referral bonuses, car leasing options and much more!

At NRI Planit, you’ll push the boundaries of quality engineering, work with brilliant minds, and see the difference your expertise makes across NZ's top systems - fast, reliable, and intelligent. Don’t worry if you don’t meet every requirement listed - we value attitude, experience and a can-do attitude above all else, and you may just be the perfect fit for this role or another within NRI Planit.

NRI Australia & New Zealand is committed to building a culturally diverse and inclusive workplace and strongly encourages applications regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability.

title: Energy Efficiency & Sustainability Specialist
description:
This Opportunity

WSP USA is seeking a highly motivated Energy Efficiency & Sustainability Specialist to lead the delivery of energy efficiency, building performance, retro-commissioning, decarbonization, and mechanical building systems projects for commercial, institutional, and industrial clients. This role combines technical expertise, project leadership, client relationship management, financial oversight, and team development to ensure successful project execution and exceptional client service.

Your Impact

Project Leadership & Delivery

title: Non-Train Control Systems (Non-TCS) Deputy Design Manager
description:
This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Non-Train Control Systems (Non-TCS) Deputy Design Manager to support the 6th Avenue / 63rd Street Communications Based Train Control (CBTC) Project in New York. The position will work under PMC’s Non-TCS Design Manager and will provide technical leadership, coordination, and oversight of the Design-Builder’s non-train-control design, procurement, installation, testing, commissioning, and closeout activities.

The Non-TCS Manager will lead oversight across mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, architectural, uninterruptible power supply (UPS), fire alarm, utility/civil, instrumentation and controls, equipment-room infrastructure, and other supporting systems that are not part of the train control system. The role will help ensure that the Design-Builder’s non-TCS work is coordinated with CBTC/TCS, communications, track, traction power, operations, safety, quality, and maintainability requirements.

The ideal candidate combines multidisciplinary design-management experience with practical knowledge of rail-transit infrastructure and design-build delivery. The candidate must be able to direct discipline reviewers, assess interfaces and constructability, identify risks early, and provide clear recommendations to the Program Management Team and MTA stakeholders.

Your Impact

  • Oversee the Design-Builder’s non-TCS design and implementation activities for mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, architectural, UPS, fire alarm, utility/civil, instrumentation and controls, equipment rooms, cabinets, racks, supports, grounding, environmental controls, and related systems.

  • Direct and coordinate multidisciplinary technical reviewers and subject-matter experts; consolidate comments and confirm that review responses are clear, consistent, timely, and aligned with contract requirements.

  • Review Design-Builder submittals, design packages, calculations, specifications, drawings, shop drawings, RFIs, technical memoranda, construction work plans, test procedures, and closeout documentation for technical completeness and compliance.

  • Perform additional responsibilities as required to support safe, compliant, timely, and coordinated delivery of the non-TCS scope.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, civil, structural, architectural engineering, architecture, construction management, systems engineering, or a related field.

  • 10+ years of relevant post-education experience in multidisciplinary infrastructure design, design management, construction management, or engineering oversight, including transit and rail experience.

  • Demonstrated experience managing or overseeing multiple building and infrastructure disciplines, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, and architectural systems.

  • Experience with transit facilities, stations, tunnels, equipment rooms, power distribution, UPS systems, grounding/bonding, fire alarm/life-safety systems, ventilation, drainage, utilities, and supporting civil works.

  • Experience coordinating with field inspectors to ensure field installations adhere to the design

  • Experience reviewing design-builder or contractor deliverables for contract compliance, constructability, interdisciplinary coordination, installation readiness, and maintainability.

  • Working knowledge of design-build project delivery, technical submittal and RFI workflows, configuration/change control, and design-review processes.

  • Ability to interpret plans, specifications, calculations, codes, standards, schedules, interface documents, and testing/commissioning requirements.

  • Strong leadership, coordination, written communication, meeting facilitation, and issue-resolution skills.

  • Ability to work effectively with designers, contractors, construction teams, agency stakeholders, operations and maintenance personnel, and Authorities Having Jurisdiction.

  • Ability to adapt to changing project priorities and work schedules. Occasional off-hours work and travel to project sites may be required.

Technical Knowledge

  • Multidisciplinary coordination of architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire alarm/life safety, UPS, utility/civil, and instrumentation and controls systems.

  • Building and equipment-room infrastructure supporting railway systems, including space planning, heat-load management, HVAC, drainage, fire protection, power quality, grounding/bonding, cable routing, access, and maintainability.

  • Interface management between non-TCS infrastructure and CBTC/train control equipment, communications systems, traction power, track, existing facilities, and operational constraints.

  • Design-review methods, constructability and installation sequencing, commissioning readiness, asset turnover, and operations and maintenance requirements.

  • Applicable New York City and New York State codes and generally recognized transit, electrical, mechanical, structural, fire/life-safety, and accessibility requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in engineering, architecture, construction management, or a related field.

  • Experience supporting MTA Construction & Development and New York City Transit projects.

  • Experience on complex brownfield rail-transit projects with active passenger service, constrained access, multiple interfaces, and staged cutovers.

  • Experience leading technical teams on design-build programs and supporting change management, risk management, claims avoidance, and schedule recovery.

  • Familiarity with requirements-management, document-control, and project-management systems used on major infrastructure programs.

title: Postdoctoral Researcher
company: Botnar Institute of Immune Engineering - BIIE
description:
The group of Prof. Georg Seelig is seeking a highly skilled and innovative researcher with experience in performing and analyzing massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in engineering human cells (e.g. through genome editing, CAR or similar transgene integration etc). The candidate will also have experience in machine learning-guided design of proteins or cis-regulatory elements and related methods. This role involves the design of novel mRNA, gene or cell therapies with increased specificity.

Principal Responsibilities

  • Designing and testing of synthetic cis-regulatory elements and other modalities for targeting activity of an mRNA or gene-based expression system to specific cell types.
  • Genome engineering of human immune cells.
  • Designing and performing massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) with sequencing readouts to identify cis-regulatory elements that result in high mRNA stability, cell type or state-specific expression or similar.
  • Developing and applying approaches for performing MPRAs in primary immune cells.
  • Developing and applying novel single-cell analysis techniques including readout of reporter assays.
  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams to advance testing of nucleic acid therapeutics.
  • Analyzing data, preparing detailed reports, planning follow-on experiments, and presenting findings to internal teams and at scientific conferences.
  • Staying abreast of latest developments in genomics, synthetic immunology and related topics to continuously improve methodologies and outcomes.
  • Preparing technical reports, summaries, protocols, and quantitative analyses.
  • Composing scientific manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and patent applications.
  • Helping train and mentor junior scientists and technical staff.

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering, Bioengineering or a related field.
  • Proven track record in performing sequencing-based high throughput assays (MPRAs, Sort-seq, etc.) to identify functional protein variants, cis-regulatory elements or to characterize transcription factors.
  • Strong background in molecular biology and mammalian cell work, ideally including work with primary human immune cells or induced pluripotent stem cells.
  • Experience with next generation sequencing, flow cytometry and related high throughput techniques.
  • Strong track record in applying bioinformatics workflows for analysis of sequencing data.
  • Proven experience with data science, python programming, machine learning and related techniques.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex scientific data to diverse audiences.
  • Ability to work independently and constructively as part of a team in a collaborative scientific environment.
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills, with a proactive approach to overcoming research and project challenges.

ABOUT STANFORD UNIVERSITY AND RESIDENTIAL & DINING ENTERPRISES:

Stanford University is one of the world's leading teaching and research universities. Founded in 1891, Stanford’s mission is to create and share knowledge and to prepare students to be curious, to think critically, and to contribute to the world. With world-class scholars and seven schools located together on a single campus, Stanford offers academic excellence across the broadest array of disciplines including business, education, engineering, humanities and sciences, law, medicine, and sustainability. It also is an engine of innovation, blending theory and practice to move ideas and discoveries from labs and classrooms out into the world. Stanford strives to foster a culture of expansive inquiry, fresh thinking, searching discussion, and freedom of thought – preparing students for leadership and engaged citizenship in the world. The university is located between San Francisco and San Jose in the heart of California's Silicon Valley, on a scenic 8,180-acre campus.

Residential & Dining Enterprises (R&DE), the largest auxiliary organization at Stanford University, supports the academic mission of the university by providing high-quality services to students and other members of the university community. R&DE has an annual operating budget of $400M, operates 24/7/365, and oversees a $3B asset portfolio comprising over 7 million square feet—one-third of the campus footprint. R&DE provides housing for 16,000 students and dependents, serves 8 million meals annually at 48 student dining venues and 32 culinary enterprises. In addition, R&DE provides executive services, conference operations, and guest lodging. R&DE is a talented and diverse team of 1,200+ who comprise the following divisions: Student Housing Operations & Stanford Conferences; Stanford Dining and Hospitality & Auxiliaries; Maintenance Operations and Capital Projects; and a team of R&DE strategic business partners—Finance & Administration, Information Technology, Human Resources, and Strategic Communications and Marketing.

“Students (Customers) First” is R&DE’s mantra and its strategic goals reflect its commitment to delivering service excellence to the campus community. R&DE’s belief is “students are never an interruption in our day; they are the reason we are here. ”R&DE’s dedication to promoting fair treatment, access to opportunities, and a positive work environment is reflected in its essential priorities and efforts for cultivating a culture of operational excellence as a foundational cornerstone. R&DE is committed to creating and sustaining inclusive excellence where all staff feel a sense of belonging and are empowered to thrive.

ADVERTISING TITLE: CORRECTIONAL SENTENCE TECHNICIAN-F/C

This open competitive advertisement is for a Career Service position located at Gadsden Correctional Institution in the Classification Department.

The Classification Department assesses and classifies inmates based on their needs, risks, and behaviors. We ensure appropriate housing and program placements within the correctional system. Our goal is to enhance safety and security while promoting effective rehabilitation, ultimately aiding in the successful reintegration of inmates into society.

This position is not a telework position and is required to report to the FDC office in the area it serves.

JOB DUTIES:

  • Look at commitment documents to understand sentencing rules, update sentence information, and make sure release dates are correct. Check computer calculations and manually calculate jail time credit, informing staff of any changes.
  • Work with Public Defenders, State Attorneys, Sheriffs, and Court Clerks to fix mistakes in commitment documents and clear up any confusion about sentences. Follow up to make sure all needed documents are received and processed.
  • Search the inmate information system to find and fix errors in inmate identification and number assignments, making sure the correct sentence details are entered in the Offender Based Information System (OBIS).
  • Review new commitments after inmate intake to decide if a new inmate number is needed or if they can use their original number. Make necessary changes to sentence details and recalculate release dates, informing the Central Office of any updates.
  • Work with Central Office staff to identify repeat offenders and document post-release supervision violations, creating a detailed paperwork trail for accountability and making changes to policies and procedures related to sentence structure issues.

Join us in this dynamic role where attention to detail and effective communication make a significant impact on the justice system!

title: IT Support Specialist III

title: Senior Systems Engineer, Wintel

  • Generate infrastructure reporting

description:

title: Lead Professional, Structural Engineering
description:
This Opportunity

Provides high level technical assistance and guidance for multi-site/phase due diligence, investigation, remediation, improvement, and/or construction of building and infrastructure projects in the public and private sector. Tasks include the research, design, concept development, planning, and construction of load-bearing structures or structural elements, such as buildings bridges, roadways, and mechanical structures. Substantiates reports and documentation to advise on material, installation, design, and construction specifications. Ensures that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards for design, safety, structural soundness, and functionality.

Your Impact
  • Provide guidance with collecting, compiling, and analyzing data from the physical work site, surveys, blueprints, GIS data, subsurface utility information, maps, hydrologic analysis, geotechnical data, and other matrices for project development, design, and construction.
  • Apply high-level structural and civil engineering techniques and processes to identify improvements for various infrastructure project phases including concept development, preliminary design, final design, procurement, construction, and operation.
  • Perform professional structural engineering work and conduct research and inspections of proposed and existing site conditions, resources, buildings, infrastructure, transportation channels, and operations to determine conformance with applicable rules, standards, and construction or operating permits.
  • Develop construction plans, specifications, and cost estimates; preparing construction safety and phasing plans, and updating infrastructure layout plans that require coordination with owners, other disciplines, sub-consultants, and clients.
  • Involved from project inception to completion in the management of design, construction, rehabilitation, and remediation of building and infrastructure projects, ensuring durability of materials and structural soundness from loads and pressures caused by environmental or human influence.
  • Develop and incorporate advanced technologies, monitoring devices, building materials, modeling techniques, design requirements, and operating strategies to account for the safety and functionality of end-users, transportation vehicles/systems, and implementing future-ready solutions with structural and civil engineering design standards.
  • Oversee and monitor cross-functional teams of engineers, architects, planners, and scientific professionals to execute project work on mid-level and/or multiple concurrent projects, including budgets, tracking hours and expenses, task completion, cost and quantities of materials/equipment/labor, technical calculations, permit applications, construction, compliance documentation, and regulatory and technical analysis memos.
  • Coordinate, review and approve building and infrastructure design plans, ensuring data integrity and work is compliant with all applicable codes, ordinances, and regulations.
  • Prepare data and visualizations such as tables, charts, reports, sketches, calculations, cross-sections, and 2D/3D illustrations for the interpretation or presentation of more complex data, findings, or analyses.
  • Prepare comprehensive technical reports and presentations that explain research, concepts, and recommendations to prevent, control, restore, or address structural, environmental, design, and/or construction issues or opportunities.
  • Analyze, evaluate, and interpret data obtained during site investigations, offering input with developing action plans for moderate- to high-level risk mitigation activities.
  • Prepare and implement site Health and Safety Plans (HASPs).
  • Interact with regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and clients in a confident and professional manner
  • Proactively collaborate with other engineers, professionals, and infrastructure authorities on Federal, State, regional, local, and privately funded improvement and development projects, as well as proposal and business development opportunities.
  • Remain current in latest structural engineering techniques and practices.
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.
Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Structural or Civil Engineering, or closely related discipline.
  • 7 to 10 years of relevant post education experience in engineering discipline and prior structural or civil design experience.
  • Engineer license required.
  • Proficient with structural engineering principles, practices, process, design/build, and the application to project work-related issues.
  • Knowledge and experience with infrastructure planning, design, and construction management; including active involvement in a variety of rehabilitation, new design, and construction projects.
  • Working knowledge with process and concepts for sustainability, and reducing and eliminating the use or generation of hazardous substances/greenhouse gas.
  • Well-defined specific knowledge of relevant structural and civil construction laws, codes, regulations, compliance practices, and record-keeping requirements.
  • Well-developed ability to make technical computations and calculations involving the application of engineering principles, understanding plans and specifications, and making factual comparisons to the appropriate regulations.
  • Ability to plan and conduct inspections and investigations on various aspects of the construction and design of buildings, facilities, or structures, applying applicable regulations and policies
  • Highly effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
  • Demonstrated high-level of self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
  • Works independently with minimal oversight and provides guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
  • Highly proficient with technical writing, office automation, discipline-specific design software (i.e., MicroStation, AutoCAD, Civil 3D, ArcGIS, InRoads, Geopak, GeoSlope, ANSYS, STADD, HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS), technology, math principles, physics, predictive models, spreadsheets, and tools.
  • Well-developed critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to apply technical knowledge to reach conclusions from testing results, data collation, computations, statistical analysis and arriving at the most effective, economical, and logical solution.
  • Demonstrated effectiveness at coordinating and assertively directing subcontractors and others to consistently complete tasks safely and efficiently.
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
  • Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
  • Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree in Engineering.
  • 40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.
  • Basic First Aid and Adult CPR training desired.

WSP Benefits:
WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Expected Salary: $103,300 -$153,670

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

title: Programme Analyst (Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants)_(Nationals Only)
description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background and Organizational Context

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Cuba works closely with the Government and other national stakeholders to support the country’s national development priorities in alignment with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

The Executive Board of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has approved the new Country Programme Document for Cuba, which will guide the agency’s cooperation with the country from 2026 to 2030.

The areas of focus include economic recovery and productive transformation, environmental management and disaster risk reduction, social protection programs and services, and the strengthening of institutions and modernization of public administration.

Strategic themes addressed by this roadmap include development financing, including environmental aspects; efforts to achieve robust statistics, with an emphasis on integrated vulnerability measurement; capacity building for macroeconomic management; and digital transformation with equity, with particular attention to implementation of services for the population.

The Programme promotes developing capacities for decentralization, ICT usage to digital transformation, low-carbon models in sectors and communities, targeted support for vulnerabilities, as well as a broad health and development approach.

Other topics reflected include nature-positive and low-carbon development, adoption of circularity principles, a just energy transition, risk management, disaster risk reduction and climate resilience, preparedness and response, food security, social protection, equity and non-discrimination, and care services.

The Programme Unit works to support achievement of UNDP strategic objectives to create a world where people and planet thrive together, and to help the Country Office act with both ambition and scale to address urgent problems facing the country as well as global climate deteriorating conditions. Programme staff assist the Country Office in formulating and implementing programme strategies that go beyond solving immediate development challenges to create future smart and integrated systemic changes in resilience and capacity building within the country.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the ARR(P) or Programme Specialist, the Programme Analyst analyzes political, social and economic trends and participates in the formulation, management and evaluation of programme activities within assigned portfolio and thematic area.

The Programme Analyst may supervise and lead programme support staff. The Programme Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme and Operations teams in the CO, programme staff in other UN Agencies, UNDP staff in HQs and Regional Hubs, external specialists, and government partners to ensure successful implementation of the UNDP programme.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

1.) Contribute to the formulation and implementation of programme strategies and policies.
Example of Duties:
  • Provide inputs to thorough analysis of the political, social and economic situation in the country; provides collaborative inputs to the UN Common Country Assessment and Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNCCA and UNSDCF) as well as to the preparation/revision of the Country Programme Document (CPD), Integrated Work Plan (IWP) and other strategic documents.
  • Provide inputs to operationalize UNSDCF/ CPD in collaboration with the main partners and other UN Agencies.
  • Ensure implementation of relevant programme Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure the effectiveness CO business processes.
  • Analyze and synthesize proposals in assigned programme areas.

2.) Participate in effective management of the CO programme within the assigned thematic/sector areas focusing on quality assurance and risk management from formulation to implementation of the country programme.

Example of Duties:
  • Provide input to design and formulation of CO programmes, translate UNDP priorities into local interventions, and oversee programme implementation with the implementing partners within the assigned programme areas. Ensure that design and formulation of programme considers societal digital technology risks and opportunities and other future signals.
  • Oversee planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring of the assigned programme areas; and track use of financial resources in accordance with UNDP rules and regulations. Ensure digital technology solutions in programme implementation are managed towards scalability and sustainability in line with UNDP’s digital standards.
  • Ensure effective application of results-based management tools and track achievement of strategic results.
  • Ensure the effective use of data in programme implementation, across the data lifecycle; and support effective monitoring, evaluation and learning on programme impact.
  • Provide inputs to trends analysis for future informed and anticipatory programming.
  • Support preparation for audits and the implementation of management responses.
  • Prepare inputs for reporting, including donor and corporate reports.
  • Support the rollout of new initiatives and programmes including through presentation of the project to PAC, finalize contribution agreements, and determine required revisions.

3.) Support creation of strategic partnerships and implementation of the CO resource mobilization strategy.
Example of Duties:
  • Support development of partnerships with the UN Agencies, international financial institutions (IFIs), government institutions, donors, private sector (if applicable to CO), and civil society in assigned programme/ thematic areas.
  • Provide input in Identifying strategic programme areas of cooperation, including for joint programming.
  • Analyze and research information on donors, prepare substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation, identify opportunities for initiation of new projects, and support Country Office resource mobilization efforts.
  • Contribute to development of portfolios and Country office pipeline including through the design of Programme/Project documents, concept notes, proposals and cross-sectoral coordination in assigned areas to bring resources for projects.

4.) Support Provision of top-quality advisory services to the Government and facilitate knowledge building and management.

Example of Duties:
  • Identify policy-driven issues; and identify and compile best practices and lessons learned directly linked to programme country policy goals.
  • Support establishment and strengthening of national and international advocacy networks. Implement relevant, high -impact advocacy with key partners.
  • Support development of policies and institutions to address country problems and needs in collaboration with the Government and other strategic partners.
  • Ensure that policy advisory contributes to inclusive societal digital transformation and takes digital technology risks and opportunities or futures signals into account.
  • Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks, communities of practice, and digital knowledge platforms.
  • Organize training for the operations/ projects staff on programme related matters in assigned programme areas.
5.)
Example of Duties:
The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization
Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: May supervise Programme support staff

Requirements

Education

  • Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Economics, Political Sciences, Social Sciences, or related field is required or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

  • Up to 2 years (with master’s degree) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national and/or international level in providing management advisory services and hands-on experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development portfolios and projects within assigned thematic area.
  • Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP.

Desirable criteria

  • Work experience in an international organization and knowledge of UNDP policies and procedures.
  • Project management.

Proven ability to work effectively in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams.

Language requirements

  • Fluency in the UN language of the duty station is required.
  • Fluency in the national language of the duty station is required for local staff.
  • Fluency in Spanish and English is required.

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

title: Administrative Associate
description:
This position has been deemed critical by the School of Humanities and Sciences Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring freeze.

Work Arrangement: This position is on-site only, based on the Stanford campus

Budgeted Salary: The budgeted base salary range for this position is $37.12 to $39.14 per hour.

The School of Humanities and Sciences (H&S) is the foundation of a liberal arts education at Stanford. The school encompasses 24 departments and 25 interdisciplinary programs. H&S is home to fundamental and applied research, where free, open, and critical inquiry is pursued across disciplines. As the university’s largest school, H&S serves as the foundation of a Stanford undergraduate education no matter which discipline students pursue as a major. Graduate students work alongside world-renowned faculty to pursue and shape foundational research that leads to breakthroughs and discoveries that shed new light on the past, influence the present, and shape the future. Together, faculty and students in H&S engage in inspirational teaching, learning, and research every day.

Department/Program Description:

Since its founding in 1980, the Stanford Humanities Center (The Center) has been sponsoring advanced research into the historical, philosophical, literary, artistic, and cultural dimensions of the human experience. It is an independent research center reporting to the Dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences. The Center's annual fellows, international visitors, research workshops, and annual public events strengthen the intellectual and creative life of the university and foster innovative and interdisciplinary scholarship and teaching. The Center for Spatial and Textual Analysis (CESTA), part of the Humanities Center, embraces emerging digital methodologies and tools to complement existing traditional research methods of analysis and interpretation. CESTA’s interdisciplinary research

projects explore places, global spaces, texts, textual artefacts, data visualization, digital curation, preservation and display, linked data and interoperability, and sustainability. As a scholarly community, CESTA supports and encourages cutting-edge work across the humanities and the interpretative social sciences. Through research projects, programs, seminars, workshops and informal initiatives, CESTA is dedicated to nurturing, training and professionalizing scholars of the future from a variety of disciplines, who will learn how to ask and answer data-driven questions focused on cultural, environmental, historical, social, and textual issues. Together, the Stanford Humanities Center and CESTA serve as the hub for an international network of fellows, visiting scholars, students, and alumni.

Position Summary

The Stanford Humanities Center (the Center) and the School of H&S Dean’s Office (HSDO) are seeking to hire an experienced and highly motivated Administrative Associate who will be a member of the Center staff and the HSDO admin staff. The position is split evenly between the two organizations, but it’s primary reporting is to the CESTA Programs Manager and who will work under the general supervision of the Executive Director and CESTA Faculty Director.

The Administrative Associate will process CESTA transactions, including financial, procurement, human resources, research grant, and student aid, in systems such as Stanford Financial Systems, Graduate Financial Services, Sequoia, and others. In collaboration with the Center’s Senior Manager of Finance and Operations, this role is responsible for arranging travel, submitting and processing travel expenses and reimbursements, procuring goods and services and verifying purchases using the purchasing card, reconciling expenditures against operating and grant budgets, tracking expenditures against program budgets, monitoring the use and documentation of PCard transactions. This role is responsible for collecting and organizing student data required for hiring/terminating/updating students records in the system. The role supports the CESTA Programs Manager, who will be the students’ hiring manager in Sequoia.

During their time in Humanities and Science Dean’s Office (HSDO), the Administrative Associate will work directly with the Executive Assistant to the Dean. In this role they will assist in processing financial transactions, coordinating small events involving the Dean, and managing the Dean’s filing. In addition, the job involves some office management including ordering supplies, greeting guests and working closely with the HSDO admin team.

This is a three-year, fixed term, benefits eligible position that begins on the start date and may be renewable in the future based on programmatic need and funding availability.

This is a 100% FTE, non-exempt position split 50% for CESTA and 50% for the H&S Dean’s Office. This position will be based on the Stanford campus, and it is expected to be fully on-site.

The ideal candidate will be a motivated and friendly individual with experience in higher education administration, capable of processing a wide array of financial and Human Resources transactions. Strong organizational, planning and execution skills are critical for this position and the ability to work independently or as part of a team.

To apply, please submit a brief cover letter outlining qualifications and work experience and current CV. Thank you for considering employment opportunities with the School of Humanities and Sciences.

Preferred Requirements

  • Prior experience with Stanford systems is preferred but not required.

Core Duties:

  • Respond to inquiries, and determine and take appropriate action as required. Serve as a resource regarding a defined set of policies and procedures.

  • Perform duties associated with scheduling, organizing, and operating conferences, seminars, and events, including recommending vendors for services, overseeing the production and distribution of materials, coordinating logistics, and serving as liaison with internal and external vendors.

  • Draft and/or generate routine communications; coordinate production (formatting, copying, etc.) and dissemination of documents, such as presentations, course handouts, grant proposals, conference and seminar materials, reports, brochures, and displays.

  • Plan and schedule calendar(s) based on consultation, resolve calendaring conflicts, and arrange travel in compliance with unit, university, and sponsor policies.

  • Process and monitor routine financial transactions, which may include researching and resolving discrepancies.

  • Maintain office supplies and equipment; obtain vendor quotations, as needed. Coordinate office moves.

  • May serve as the point of contact for general maintenance, health and safety, and other facility concerns within the unit(s); report any incidents or potential safety problems to appropriate representatives. Track completion of required training.

  • Maintain approved content on websites.

  • May perform human resources transactional support, e.g. time cards, I9s, and/or faculty affairs support.

  • May guide and train student and/or contingent workers including scheduling, assigning, and prioritizing workloads, setting appropriate deadlines, and reviewing work for quality and timeliness.

Minimum Education and Experience

High school diploma and three years of administrative experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Demonstrated success in following through and completing routine tasks.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to prioritize and multi-task.

title: Project Manager - Power & Energy
description:
Project Manager – Power & Energy

Locations: Sydney | Newcastle | Brisbane | Adelaide

The Opportunity

WSP’s Power & Energy team is growing, and we’re looking for an experienced Project Manager to support the delivery of major power infrastructure projects across Australia.

Based in Sydney, Newcastle, Brisbane or Adelaide, you’ll manage multidisciplinary projects across transmission, distribution and substation infrastructure, renewables and/or power generation working closely with our engineering teams, clients and project partners.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of projects from early planning and design through to delivery and close-out, balancing the technical, commercial and client-facing aspects of project management.

You’ll join a collaborative national team and contribute to a growing pipeline of work supporting Australia’s evolving energy and power infrastructure needs.

What you’ll do

As a Project Manager within our Power & Energy team, you will:

  • Lead multidisciplinary teams delivering transmission, distribution and substation, renewables and power generation projects.
  • Manage projects across the full lifecycle, from proposals and project initiation through engineering, delivery and close-out.
  • Develop and manage project scope, budgets, schedules, forecasts and resourcing plans.
  • Monitor project financial performance, including costs, margins, invoicing, cash flow and forecasting.
  • Manage project risks, changes and commercial matters, identifying issues early and driving practical solutions.
  • Coordinate engineering, design, project controls, procurement and other disciplines to support successful project delivery.
  • Establish appropriate project governance, reporting, quality and safety requirements.
  • Build strong relationships with clients and act as a key point of contact throughout project delivery.
  • Support contract negotiations, scope development, project proposals and commercial discussions.
  • Work closely with technical and discipline leads to ensure engineering deliverables meet project, client and quality requirements.
  • Coordinate internal resources, specialist expertise, suppliers and subcontractors as required.
  • Provide clear project reporting on programme, budget, risk, scope and overall performance.
  • Support lessons learned and project close-out activities to continuously improve how we deliver our work.
  • Contribute to the continued growth and development of WSP’s Power & Energy business in Australia.

About you

We’re looking for someone who combines strong project management capability with an understanding of engineering and infrastructure delivery.

Ideally, you will bring:

  • A tertiary qualification in Engineering, Project Management or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant industry experience.
  • Approximately 4+ years’ experience across engineering, infrastructure or project delivery environments.
  • Demonstrated project management experience within power, energy, utilities or major infrastructure.
  • Experience delivering transmission, distribution, substations or other complex electrical infrastructure projects will be highly regarded.
  • A strong understanding of the project lifecycle, including planning, design, procurement, delivery, commissioning and close-out.
  • Experience managing budgets, programmes, forecasts, project controls, risks and commercial outcomes.
  • Strong commercial awareness and an ability to understand the relationship between technical delivery and project financial performance.
  • Experience coordinating multidisciplinary engineering teams, consultants, contractors and other project stakeholders.
  • Strong client relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent communication, organisation and problem-solving capability.
  • A collaborative leadership style and the confidence to take ownership of project outcomes.
  • A strong commitment to health, safety, quality and sustainable project delivery.
  • Flexibility to undertake occasional project or client travel as required.

How You’ll Work

You can be based in one of our offices across Australia, including Brisbane, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Sydney, Newcastle or Adelaide. working closely with local project teams while collaborating with our national Transmission & Distribution specialists.

The role offers a mix of office, site and hybrid working, giving you exposure to local projects as well as major programs across Australia.

Imagine a Better Future

Imagine a future where your work contributes directly to a cleaner, more connected and resilient Australian energy system.

At WSP, you’ll have the opportunity to apply your transmission lines expertise to complex engineering challenges while building a career with a global professional services business.

Whether you’re looking to take the next step technically, broaden your project exposure, or move into senior technical and leadership responsibilities, we’d love to hear from you.

Because with us, you can.

Ready to Apply?

Apply today via the link provided and help shape the future of Australia’s energy networks.

Questions?
For a confidential discussion about our Transmission Lines opportunities, please contact Carmina Navalta from our Talent Acquisition team.

title: IT Support Specialist III
location: North Las Vegas, NV, United States
description:
Are you a highly skilled and motivated IT professional passionate about delivering exceptional technical support and enhancing user productivity within a critical national security environment? The Information Technology Directorate at the Nevada National Security Sites (NNSS) in North Las Vegas is seeking a high-performing individual to join our dynamic Service Desk team as an IT Support Specialist III. In this critical role, you will leverage your expertise to resolve complex technical challenges, optimize IT operations, and contribute to a seamless technology experience for our vital mission.

About Our Team: Our Service Desk is the heart of IT support at the NNSS, dedicated to providing rapid, effective, and customer-centric solutions to support national security initiatives. We foster a collaborative environment where innovation and problem-solving are celebrated, and continuous learning is encouraged. Join us in our mission to empower our users with reliable and cutting-edge technology that underpins the NNSS's crucial contributions to national security.

Key Responsibilities

  • Advanced Technical Support & Resolution:
    • Serve as a Tier III expert, diagnosing and resolving the most difficult and advanced user-facing hardware, software, and network issues, minimizing downtime and ensuring business continuity for NNSS operations.
    • Manage and prioritize client requests and issues efficiently through our ticketing system, providing timely support via call, chat, and in-person interactions.
    • Conduct in-depth analysis of recurring problems to identify root causes and implement sustainable solutions, proactively preventing future issues within the NNSS infrastructure.
  • System Optimization & Deployment:
    • Lead the installation, configuration, and upgrading of diverse hardware, operating systems, and application software, ensuring optimal performance and compatibility across NNSS systems.
    • Oversee equipment relocation and setup, minimizing disruption to user workflow at the North Las Vegas facility.
    • Monitor the operation and performance of critical hardware and software systems, identifying and addressing potential vulnerabilities or inefficiencies.
    • Administer and manage Microsoft Office 365 services and their various functions, including user provisioning, security configurations, and advanced feature utilization, to enhance collaboration and productivity.
  • Account Management and Compliance:
    • Awareness of license agreements for critical software (e.g., Microsoft, Adobe, MathWorks), ensuring cost-effectiveness and adherence to Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSS specific requirements.
    • Maintain and update Active Directory distribution groups, facilitating efficient user and resource management.
    • Maintain and update our Office 365 Instance
  • Process Improvement & Documentation:
    • Develop and modify IT processes and procedures to enhance efficiency, streamline operations, and improve service delivery within the NNSS IT environment.
    • Prepare clear, concise, and comprehensive documentation, procedures, and reports for IT systems and administrative functions.
  • Training & Mentorship:
    • Develop and deliver engaging user training programs on hardware, software, and IT best practices, empowering NNSS users to maximize their technology.

    • Monitor conformance to IT plans and initiatives, ensuring objectives are met.
    • Report technical problems, development issues, and related activities to management, providing clear insights and actionable recommendations.
